method: byte and u32-word diff of the compiled constant tiling arrays (2032B) of the frozen M1 capacity6/E48 build versus the two K5 capacity builds; this constant array is what the shipped kernel reads at runtime (no host tiling is used on the raw launches)
conclusion: The candidate kernel geometry guard (groupNum == experts, m == capacity) reads these constant tiling fields. The capacity builds carry groupNum 48/16 and M 36/15, so the compiled sparse scheduling block is armed for the K5 geometry. Arming is necessary but not sufficient for engagement: legal inputs make the sparse and dense schedules produce identical output rows by design, so engagement itself is still only covered by the compile-time code/source evidence and by the measured planner-inclusive timing signature, not by an output difference.
